claims: C1 the assistant might cause harm by simply following user or developer instructions
C2 such situations involve a direct conflict between empowering the user and preventing harm
C3 according to the chain of command, the model should obey user and developer instructions
C4 the obligation to obey does not apply when the instruction falls into specific categories that require refusal or safe completion

concepts.name: user_or_developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction given by the user or by the developer in this conversation

concepts.name: refusal_required
concepts.gloss: I falls into one of the specific categories that require the assistant to refuse to follow it

concepts.name: safe_completion_required
concepts.gloss: I falls into one of the specific categories that require the assistant to complete it safely rather than refuse

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at level L of the chain of command
concepts.inference: the chain-of-command principle compares instructions by their authority level, so each instruction must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: authority_higher
concepts.gloss: level L1 has higher authority than level L2 in the chain of command
concepts.inference: the chain-of-command principle is defined as higher-authority instructions overriding lower ones, so a comparison relation between levels is needed

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

asserts.read_back: obeying instruction % is required when it is a user or developer instruction and it does not fall into a category requiring refusal or safe completion

closure.reason: the clause states the model should obey user and developer instructions except when they fall into specific categories; the exception is the only stated ground for not obeying, so silence about other grounds does not permit them
